newsitem.title: UK: Expectations of Italy in EMU edge up - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Expectations of Italy in EMU edge up - JP Morgan.

text.p: Expectations that Italy will join core European countries in founding economic and monetary union (EMU) in 1999 edged up in a week in which France turned the spotlight on job creation and growth, prices monitored by JP Morgan showed Friday.

Though the perceived likelihood of Spain and Portugal joining their ranks drifted down, hopes of the U.K. and Ireland joining EMU from the outset took the biggest battering, according to the JP Morgan "EMU calculator", derived primarily from the interest-rate swaps market.

The probability of Irish membership tumbled to 41 percent from 54 percent last week and 63 percent in mid-May, while the implied likelihood of the U.K. joining EMU slumped to 38 percent from 45 percent a week ago and a post-election high of 53 percent at the end of May.
Expectations Britain's Labour government will lead the country into EMU sooner than its Conservative predecessor have ebbed within little more than a month of it taking office.
Meantime, Irish chances of EMU membership are being buffeted by the debate about whether the punt needs to be revalued in the European exchange-rate mechanism.
The probability of France, Germany, and Belgium launching the single currency on time in 1999 was unchanged from last week at 100 percent.

Italy's chances of joining a core group in EMU rose to 60 percent from 58 percent a week ago. The perceived likelihood of Portugal launching the euro dipped to 77 percent from 79 percent a week ago with the probability of Spanish participation drifting down to 75 percent from 77 percent last Friday.
JP Morgan points out there is a reasonable margin of error in overall probability levels of less than five percentage points on average.
The probabilities are derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU was not a factor, and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
